title: Microsoft Purview: audit records for role and scoped-role permission checks
summary: The rollout details and control paths are supported, but the guidance overstates how Entra roles override scoped permissions and incorrectly says existing searches cannot include the new operations without changes. The retention discussion also overlooks published platform-wide retention rules.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licence requirement specific to the two new operations is not yet published, so the feature-specific licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview "CheckUsersInRoles" "CheckUserInRolesWithScopes" audit configuration licensing; "CheckUsersInRoles" licensing price meter. Opened audit-get-started and audit-solutions-overview; no operation-specific licence found.
claims.fix: Keep the feature-specific unknown, but add: 'The general Audit prerequisites still apply: an appropriate organisation subscription and per-user licensing are required to log and retain audit records.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-get-started#step-1-verify-organization-subscription-and-billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The audit search documentation says retention and searchability depend on the subscription and the licence assigned to specific users.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.claim: The audit search page publishes retention periods for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange and SharePoint activity.
claims.quote: the system retains audit records for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, and SharePoint activity for one year by default.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: retention
claims.claim: The applicable retention rules for the new records are unpublished, leaving open whether retention follows licensing or requires a policy.
claims.quote: Audit records for all other activities are retained for 180 days by default, or you can use audit log retention policies to configure longer retention periods.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of the retention paragraph and the retention open question with: 'General Audit retention rules apply: Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days; Audit (Premium) retains activities outside Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint for 180 days by default, subject to applicable retention policies. Non-user-entity records have a separate fixed one-year retention rule. Confirm the new records' workload and generating identity before assigning a duration.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-solutions-overview, including its non-user-entity qualification, and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-retention-policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Holding an Entra role together with a scoped Purview role group makes the user's effective permissions unscoped without qualification.
claims.quote: Entra roles always take precedence, and scoping applied through Administrative Units doesn't restrict the user's effective permissions for overlapping capabilities.
claims.fix: In both places replace the unqualified precedence explanation with: 'When an Entra role and a scoped Purview role group overlap, the Entra role takes precedence and administrative-unit scoping does not restrict effective permissions for those overlapping capabilities.' Keep the citation to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions#role-precedence-and-scope-behavior.
